missions.title: Expensive Spells
missions.story: Coach Rao slaps the clipboard. "Too many of my bowlers are leaking runs. Ujwal, how many spells in this log went for more than 8 an over?"
missions.task: On the Spells sheet, economy is column G and the data runs from row 2 to row 61. Write a formula in any cell that counts the spells with an economy above 8.
hints: You need a function that counts only the cells that meet a condition.
COUNTIF takes two parts: the range to look at, then the condition in quotes.
A condition with an operator looks like ">3" in quotes, for example =COUNTIF(A1:A10,">3"). Point it at the economy column.

missions.title: Ujwal's Wicket Tally
missions.story: Selector Mehta is shortlisting for the next tour. "Show me how many wickets Ujwal Mojidra has taken across this log. Do not count anyone else's."
missions.task: Bowler names are in column B and wickets are in column F, rows 2 to 61. Write a formula that totals the wickets taken by Ujwal Mojidra only.
hints: You want to add up one column, but only for rows where another column matches a name.
SUMIF takes three parts: the range holding the condition, the condition itself, then the range to add up.
Text conditions go in quotes, for example =SUMIF(A1:A10,"Tom",B1:B10). Match it to the bowler column, then add the wickets column.

missions.title: Ujwal's Economy Rate
missions.story: Analyst Priya is building the scouting sheet. "I need Ujwal's average economy rate, rounded to 2 decimal places. One formula, please."
missions.task: Using the economy values in column G and bowler names in column B (rows 2 to 61), write one formula that gives Ujwal Mojidra's average economy rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: Two ideas combine here: an average with a condition, wrapped in a rounding step.
AVERAGEIF works like SUMIF: condition range, condition, then the range to average. ROUND goes around the outside.
Shape: =ROUND(AVERAGEIF(condition_range, "name", value_range), digits). Fill the pieces from the bowler and economy columns.
